question: Will Bitcoin trade above $83,000 at any point between September 17 and September 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: BTC is ~$78,982 (Sep 8); $83,000 is ~5.1% above spot and above the $82,000-82,300 zone that has rejected four rallies since Aug 25. Reference class: for a random BTC date, how often does the max daily High over days t+9 to t+10 exceed 1.048x spot — ~35% at typical realized vol. A driftless lognormal touch model (sigma_daily 2.0-2.6%, window 8.7-10.7 days out) gives 0.35-0.41; Kalshi's September monthly-high board ($82.5k at 71c, $85k at 48c on Sep 4) back-solves to a lower implied vol (~1.85%/day), pulling toward the low end. The dominant structural feature is the Sep 16 FOMC decision one day before the window: hike odds are 45-70% depending on venue, so the modal path into Sep 17-18 is a hawkish outcome pressuring risk assets, while a no-hike relief pop from ~$80k would clear $83k readily. Scenario weighting (0.55 x 0.18 + 0.45 x 0.57) lands at 0.36, consistent with the model range shaded down for the hike skew and the untested resistance.

calls.reconciliation: Three disputes mattered. (1) Spot: Run 3 used Sep-7 quotes ($79.5-79.9k) giving a +4.4% barrier; the two Sep-8-dated reads (CoinGecko $78,532, CaptainAltcoin $78,982) settle it at ~$78,750 and +5.3%, so Run 3's number is biased up by a stale anchor. (2) Implied vol: Run 2 said ~2.0%/day, Run 3 ~1.55%/day, from the same Polymarket ladder. Settled by recomputing the ladder from Run 2's quoted rungs — driftless 2N(-b/sigma*sqrtT) at sigma=1.95-2.0% matches $85k/$82.5k/$80k/$87.5k/$75k/$72.5k/$70k within 1-4 points; 1.55% cannot reproduce those. Run 3's 1.55% error pushed its estimate down while its stale spot pushed it up, roughly cancelling. (3) FOMC direction: pure JUDGMENT, no evidence breaks it cleanly, but the ladder I verified is symmetric across both wings, which is direct evidence traders are NOT pricing a hawkish drift into BTC — so Run 1's explicit 0.55/0.45 hike-scenario haircut layers a directional view on top of a distribution that already embeds it. I would bet against that haircut. Adopted Run 2's calibration and Run 3's framing of the random-walk vs mean-reversion bracket, but recomputed both legs at the settled spot and sigma: 0.29 and 0.31-0.33, narrower than Run 3's 0.29-vs-0.36 spread. Unsettled: no run could retrieve Deribit IV for the Sep 18 expiry or an audited empirical tally of 2-day windows containing a +5% move from t-9, so the vol calibration rests entirely on one ladder read; and no run obtained the Yahoo resolution source's own daily rows for Sep 5-8, only vendor spot. disagreements.verdict: Recomputed both at the settled spot and sigma: GBM 0.29, mean-reverting 0.31-0.33. R3's 0.36 overshoots. The specs bracket a narrower range than either run claimed; I sit inside that bracket.

disagreements.claim: Does the four-to-six-times-rejected $81.2-82.3k shelf reduce touch odds beyond what volatility already says?
disagreements.verdict: No additional drag applied. The range-bound regime that produced those rejections is already why market-implied sigma (1.95%) sits below realized (2.4%); counting the shelf separately double-counts it.

disagreements.claim: Does the Sep 16 FOMC raise or lower the probability net?
disagreements.verdict: Slightly raises. It lands 18:00 UTC on Sep 16, ~6 hours before the window opens, so its vol concentrates into the in-window leg, and a barrier-touch profits from volatility in either direction. Worth ~+1.5pt, partly offset by Yahoo's composite High printing at or marginally below the Binance max the ladder resolves off.

calls.reference_class: BTC-USD rolling 2-calendar-day windows opening ~9 days forward, requiring the window High to clear +5.3% above spot, at the currently market-implied ~1.95%/day volatility
